title: [Day 2] Read and understand: Day 2: Deployments - The Magic of Self-Healing Applications
body:
## Day 2 Task

Read through the Day 2 email and understand the key concepts before practicing.

### Key Concepts
- Pods are ephemeral and can die at any time
- Deployments manage pods and ensure desired replica count
- Self-healing: Kubernetes automatically replaces failed pods
- ReplicaSets sit between Deployments and Pods
- Labels and selectors organize and find objects

title: [Day 2] Practice kubectl commands from Day 2
body:
## Day 2 Task

Open a terminal with access to your Kubernetes cluster and practice these commands.

### Commands to Practice
```bash
kubectl create deployment my-app --image=nginx --replicas=3
kubectl get pods
kubectl get deployment my-app
kubectl get pods --watch
kubectl delete pod <pod-name>
kubectl scale deployment my-app --replicas=5
kubectl scale deployment my-app --replicas=2
kubectl get replicaset
```

---
*Generated from KubeCraft 7-Day Kubernetes Quickstart Course*

title: [Day 2] Self-assessment: Day 2 concepts
body:
## Day 2 Task

Review what you learned and make sure you can explain each concept in your own words.

### Key Concepts
- Pods are ephemeral and can die at any time. They won't come back on their own
- Deployments manage pods and ensure your desired replica count is maintained
- Self-healing means Kubernetes automatically replaces failed pods
- Scaling lets you change replica count with a single command
- ReplicaSets are the object between Deployments and Pods
- Rolling updates deploy new versions without downtime
- Labels and selectors are how Kubernetes organizes and finds objects

---
*Generated from KubeCraft 7-Day Kubernetes Quickstart Course*

title: [Day 3] Read and understand: Day 3: Kubernetes Networking
body:
## Day 3 Task

Read through the Day 3 email and understand the key concepts before practicing.

### Key Concepts
- Pod IPs change on every restart
- Services provide stable endpoints - one address that routes to multiple pods
- Label selectors connect Services to pods based on key-value labels
- ClusterIP is internal only, default type, needs port-forward for external access
- NodePort opens a port on the node for quick external access

---
*Generated from KubeCraft 7-Day Kubernetes Quickstart Course*

title: [Day 3] Practice kubectl commands from Day 3
body:
## Day 3 Task

Open a terminal with access to your Kubernetes cluster and practice these commands.

### Commands to Practice
```bash
kubectl get pods -o wide
kubectl get deployment my-app
kubectl expose deployment my-app --port=80 --target-port=80
kubectl get services
kubectl describe service my-app
kubectl port-forward service/my-app 8080:80
kubectl delete pod <pod-name>
kubectl run test-pod --image=busybox --rm -it --restart=Never -- wget -qO- http://my-app
```

title: [Day 3] Self-assessment: Day 3 concepts
body:
## Day 3 Task

Review what you learned and make sure you can explain each concept in your own words.

### Key Concepts
- Pod IPs are ephemeral. They change on every restart.
- Services provide stable endpoints. One address that routes to multiple pods.
- Label selectors connect Services to pods based on key-value labels.
- ClusterIP is internal only. Default type, needs port-forward for external access.
- NodePort opens a port on the node for quick external access.
- DNS works inside the cluster. Pods reach services by name.
- Port-forward creates a tunnel from your laptop to the cluster.

---
*Generated from KubeCraft 7-Day Kubernetes Quickstart Course*

title: [Day 4] Read and understand: Day 4: The real way to do Kubernetes
body:
## Day 4 Task

Read through the Day 4 email and understand the key concepts before practicing.

### Key Concepts
- YAML manifests define resources declaratively
- apiVersion, kind, metadata, spec form the structure of every Kubernetes resource
- kubectl apply creates or updates resources to match the file
- Multiple resources can live in one file separated by ---
- --dry-run=client -o yaml generates YAML from commands

---
*Generated from KubeCraft 7-Day Kubernetes Quickstart Course*

title: [Day 6] Read and understand: Day 6: Making your data survive in Kubernetes
body:
## Day 6 Task

Read through the Day 6 email and understand the key concepts before practicing.

### Key Concepts
- Containers are ephemeral - data doesn't persist by default
- PersistentVolume (PV) is actual storage provisioned in the cluster
- PersistentVolumeClaim (PVC) is a request for storage
- StorageClass defines how storage is provisioned
- volumeMounts defines where to mount storage inside the container

---

title: [Day 6] Self-assessment: Day 6 concepts
body:
## Day 6 Task

Review what you learned and make sure you can explain each concept in your own words.

### Key Concepts
- Containers are ephemeral. Data doesn't persist by default.
- PersistentVolume (PV) is actual storage provisioned in the cluster.
- PersistentVolumeClaim (PVC) is a request for storage.
- StorageClass defines how storage is provisioned.
- volumeMounts defines where to mount storage inside the container.
- volumes connects pods to PVCs.
- Data survives restarts because it lives outside the container.
